A fun and heartwarming game for the whole family. The gameplay is varied enough to keep things interesting, and the locations are highly atmospheric. It’s a great choice for a couple of evenings. It needs an NG+ mode that allows for further inventory expansion; there isn't enough space for ammo, so you can't carry every weapon you have to choose what to use.

Deliciously gross, like if you took the ritual scene from Silent Hill F and made it a whole Rip and Tearing badass game. A really well written wild ride about a man going through literal hell to save his girl and fight his own demons. Combat feels really hard hitting and there's a satisfying loop to how the environments are plotted. And boy, the revolver is the best thing since god invented the flamethrower. (MoistCritikal WOOOOOOO!). The game is very functional too. The only game breaking bug I had was when the scope equipped to my revolver when I didn't even have it on and it blocked my ADS. Easily fixed by equipping the scope and then taking it off again. Other than that just the occasional funny floating gib. Also there's a guy in the club at the beginning near the DJ doing the Orange Justice dance and it made me laugh for five minutes. Mark my words, its an experience that has to be seen to be believed.

The ending will hit you as a guy, as we've all probably gone through absolute pain trying to save a self destructive girl that's only using you before. Know your worth, kings.

Hellraiser does not hold it's punches and went places I'd not expect to see in a AA budget in 2026. Where most studios are terrified of taking a risk or offending, they've done both with gruesome glee. Gamers so often say they want games like Hellraiser, so I truly hope you give it a chance.

On the story front, there was an easy opportunity to make this a camp continuation of the films from 3-11 but instead they choose to focus on a continuation of the 2nd film. And from there, exploring the depths of addiction, pleasure and pain. The Cenobites in this, are not camp. Clive Barker originally did not want 'Pin Head' (The Priest) to be the series antagonist and this takes us in the correct direction of the Cenobites being horror's most beautifully perplexing villains.

Support this. It feels like everyone who worked on this agreed to punch it to nines, no holding back. Strap in however, your suffering will be legendary.

This game is amazing. It pushes boundaries most game are afraid to push. A lot of frustrating bugs like having to refight bosses again because the game just wont let me hit the finish command after I've killed them. Also there needs to be way more save points in-between puzzles. I played this game on hard and you will literally waste 20min getting back through a puzzle just to get to the point of retrying and doing something different, or not get hit by a stupid saw. I really hope they fix that in a patch. The game really starts to become not fun at that point. Other than than that I loved this game. They for sure did the hellraiser universe right. If you are a Hellraiser 1 and 2 fan this game is a must play.

Very fun AA game that leans heavily into both old and more modern Cenobite lore, with an obviously incredible level of dedication and care for the franchise seen in the homages and parralels to the original movie - the ambient lighting and smoke, the lightning effects as the cenobites warp in and out of view, even the [[spoiler story content]] that's a direct recreation of a scene from the original.

The dodging/sidestep mechanic feels kinda rough and unimpactful during what little melee combat there is.

And as for outside-of-game issues, it has to basically redownload itself every time it gets patched, ending up with 53GB updates for a single bugfix. Not great on rural internet...

On top of Saber being all-in on AI assisted coding and development, it left enough of an ick in my mouth to pick this up elsewhere and definitely not at full price, to give as little of my money to Saber as I could.

Otherwise a game I would recommend

I'm thoroughly impressed with Hellraiser: Revival, an unexpected gem that captures the tone, atmosphere and depravity of the Hellraiser universe, translating it into a game almost perfectly.

Rather than watering down the source material or trying to make it more accessible to a wider audience, the devs fully embrace everything that makes Hellraiser so distinctive: the violence, gore, sexuality and weirdness and it's better for it.

The story is well done, and I particularly enjoyed seeing the Cenobites appear as the story unfolds. The gameplay itself is decent, if nothing particularly ground breaking. It feels like a straightforward early 2000s shooter, but the box and the powers at your disposal add some welcome variety and give the combat a bit more flavour.

Overall, Hellraiser: Revival is a pleasant surprise and a great example of a game that understands its source material. Well worth a pick up for Hellraiser or Horror fans.

One of my most anticipated games this year and well worth the wait. This is every bit the Hellraiser game fans deserve and more. Its incredibly faithful to the source material in all the right, fucked up ways. The story was very well crafted and plays into its themes far better than most of the films. The survival horror and gameplay is a mix of RE7/8 and early/late 2000s shooters, which hit all the right notes. "The Box" has fun interactions throughout the campaign and we to get see more of the Labyrinth than we've ever really seen.
In short;
If you love Hellraiser; buy this.
If you love RE 7&8 and late 2000s shooters; buy this.
The Box awaits you.

Hell raiser Revival is a breath of fresh air in a time where tons of crap is being thrown at all of us from every direction. Much to my surprise they used the UR5 engine, which nearly every single game I have played that the developers use this engine as we all have experienced at one point or another has been an un optimized terrible nightmare of crashes, massive frame drops and artifracting. This was not the case with Hell Raiser Revival. Game held steady solid frames all throughout my play through and experienced zero crashes or problems. 9/10 for me. Wish the story was a tab bit longer though. Looking forward to more future installments of this franchise later on down the road.

A visually stunning experience, but far too short for its own good.

I absolutely love Hellraiser. It’s an incredibly artistic, visually beautiful, and atmospheric experience that captures the kind of dark, disturbing fascination that makes this universe so unique. Every detail feels carefully crafted, and I genuinely appreciated the artistic direction and the amount of attention put into building its world. As someone who is deeply fascinated by the Hellraiser universe, finally getting to experience this game was something I had been looking forward to for a long time.

CONS

!!! Unfortunately , my biggest disappointment is its length. For a game I waited so long for, set in a universe I’m so passionate about, it felt painfully short. And I’m not someone who rushes through games just to reach the credits. Quite the opposite. As a hardcore fan, I took my time, examined every detail, explored as much as I could, and tried to absorb everything the game had to offer. Even so, it took me only **11 hours to finish**.

That’s what makes the whole experience bittersweet. I loved almost every moment of it, and I genuinely wish I could have spent much more time in this world. The artistic vision is there, the atmosphere is there, and the fascination is definitely there. I just wish there had been more of it. More exploration, more discoveries, and more time to immerse myself in a universe that deserves so much more.

PROS:
- nails the atmosphere
- first hour or so is very immersive
- fairly priced
- limited inventory while rewarding exploration

CONS:
- abysmal FOV (had to use mod)
- stealth is semi-broken and so is enemy AI which really hurts the immersion
- Labyrinth sections overstay their welcome and come down to boring and repetitive "trial and error" with cheap deaths
- didn't care about protagonist motivation after certain point
- very repetitive loops ("bUt AlL gAmEs aRe" - no they are not) to the point that I just watched rest of the game sped up and missed absolutely nothing
If you are a fan of the movies this is a must buy. Thankfully stays true to its roots and does not hold back one bit.

Hellraiser: Revival has such sights to show you if you're a fan of survival horror. The game competently delivers on hunting for resources, inventory management, exploration, puzzles, and tense enemy encounters, topped off with a compelling story to drive you along.

Revival is every bit as gritty as you'd expect from a Hellraiser game, and it's clear a lot of care was taken to faithfully adapt the franchise here. This is, in my opinion, the strongest entry in the franchise since the second movie. If you're a fan of Hellraiser and/or survival horror then I strongly recommend giving Revival a go.

As gore filled as Hellraiser is it was also full of some great dark humour that made me laugh out loud at points so I will start my review by saying I wish there had been more of that. The sex club after the opening section of the game was genuinely funny as was the end song for the game, if you know you know.
As for the game itself it had beautiful visuals, great soundtrack and they nailed the Hellraiser vibe perfectly. They did not over use the cenobites and every time you did see them was a welcome surprise. I loved the Chatterer sequences and I wish we had a few more of those with the other priests but that's just me being greedy.
The story was a mix of a few of the movies with a lot of nods to the first film in many ways which I enjoyed and hopefully those new to the series will go check out the films after playing. I can't say I cared that much about Aiden and Sunny but I'm not sure I was supposed to, but they served as good vehicles to move the plot forward. I did enjoy Bruno though, such a cheeky Mr Magpie.
My time with Hellraiser really had me wanting to revisit Condemned criminal origins which is no bad comparison. I hope we see another Hellraiser in the future as there are many, many stories that can be told.

An excellent first-person horror game, similar to Outlast mixed with Resident Evil Village. If you enjoyed those games, you might quite like this one. Gory, torturous and a ton of adult content. Not something you want a family member to walk in and have you try explain to them. Yet it's not just some shock value or jumpscare, there's a purpose and a storyline. Some stealth with melee and shooting. You have limited resource, repair and can craft items. Sometimes intense chases and just have to run it through turning infested corridors.

Essentially a first person Resident Evil, with a heavy BDSM and suffering influence.

I quite like it.

It's like Resident Evil, if it was a horror game.

Thought the graphic violence and gore would be too much at the start. It still is, but it fits the themes and the story so it doesn't feel out of place. Was nice to see such a bold approach. It has a nice and steady progression and just keeps getting better. Just the combat at the beginning was slow before you unlocked other stuff and the achievement system is a bit funny.

Years later, ive finally gotten around to watch the first Hellraiser movie, so you can image how excited i was, when i heard they were making a game.

From the moment i watched the first movie, i was captured by the universe, and the design of the labyrtinh along with the Cenobites. Clive Barkers work truly comes to live in this video game, that does not hold back at all!

This is THE Hellraiser game that we need, and this game will hopefully show other studios, that horror games.... are supposed to be shocking! disgusting! and question the very morals of humanity and all between.

Overall... I like the combat, narrative and the art design. Truly a beautiful game and worth a play! If you like Hellraiser, you will fall in love with the franchise, playing this game.

Now.. dont waste more time on this review..... Go play the game!
